questions.question: How does Sidekiq work as an Active Job adapter?
questions.title: Active Job Adapter (Sidekiq)
questions.direct_answer: Active Job is Rails' abstraction over job backends; Sidekiq is one adapter (others: Resque, Delayed Job). You define a job `class MailJob < ApplicationJob; def perform(user); Mailer.welcome(user).deliver_now; end; end`, enqueue it `MailJob.perform_later(user)`, and Active Job routes it to the configured backend (`config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq` in environment). Sidekiq pushes the job to Redis; a Sidekiq worker picks it up and calls perform. Benefits of the adapter abstraction: switch backends without changing job code. Sidekiq is the common choice (fast, Redis-backed, threaded). Set the adapter per-env (sidekiq in production, :inline or :async in test/dev). Queues: `queue_as :mailers` or `set(wait: 5.minutes)`. The job must be serializable (args go through JSON, so symbols/complex objects don't survive — pass IDs).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Active Job abstracts job backends and Sidekiq is one adapter (config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Passing non-serializable args (symbols/objects become strings via JSON) — pass IDs instead.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Active Job abstracts job backends; Sidekiq is one adapter (config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq). Define job < ApplicationJob; perform_later; Sidekiq runs it.

You define a job class Mail Job less-than Application Job; def perform user; Mailer dot welcome user deliver now; end; end, enqueue it Mail Job perform later user, and Active Job routes it to the configured backend (config active job queue adapter sidekiq in environment). Sidekiq pushes the job to Redis; a Sidekiq worker picks it up and calls perform. Benefits of the adapter abstraction: switch backends without changing job code. Sidekiq is the common choice (fast, Redis-backed, threaded). Set the adapter per-env (sidekiq in production, inline or async in test dev). Queues: queue as mailers or set wait 5 minutes. The job must be serializable (args go through JSON, so symbols or complex objects don't survive — pass IDs).

sections.title: Active Job + Sidekiq
sections.content:
Active Job abstracts backends; Sidekiq is one adapter. perform_later -> Redis -> worker.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  J[MailJob.perform_later] --> AJ[Active Job]
  AJ --> C[adapter: :sidekiq]
  C --> R[Redis queue]
  R --> W[Sidekiq worker]
  W --> P[job.perform]
```

sections.title: Active Job adapter
sections.content:
```ruby
# config/environments/production.rb
config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq   # Sidekiq as the backend
# test/dev: :inline (run now) or :async (in-process)

# Define a job (inherits from ApplicationJob)
class MailJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :mailers                       # which queue
  def perform(user)                       # the work to do
    Mailer.welcome(user).deliver_now
  end
end

# Enqueue (returns immediately; worker runs it later)
MailJob.perform_later(user)
MailJob.set(wait: 5.minutes).perform_later(user)   # delayed
MailJob.set(queue: :urgent).perform_later(user)    # specific queue

# Sidekiq: pushes the job to Redis; a worker pops it and calls perform.
#   MailJob.perform_later -> Active Job -> Sidekiq adapter -> Redis -> worker

# Switching backends (the abstraction): change the adapter line only.
#   :sidekiq (fast, Redis, threaded) -- common in prod
#   :resque, :delayed_job           -- other backends
#   :inline (run synchronously), :async (in-process) -- test/dev

# ARGS must be SERIALIZABLE (JSON): pass IDs, not objects.
#   BAD:  MailJob.perform_later(@user)        # whole object
#   GOOD: MailJob.perform_later(@user.id)     # then User.find(id) in perform
#   (symbols become strings; complex objects don't survive JSON)
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Passing non-serializable args (symbols/objects -> strings via JSON); pass IDs instead.
Forgetting to set the adapter per-env (test/dev need :inline or :async).
Heavy work in perform without retries (use sidekiq-retries / set retry).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Active Job is Rails' abstraction over job backends; Sidekiq is one adapter.
Define class Job < ApplicationJob; def perform(args); end; enqueue with perform_later.
Sidekiq pushes the job to Redis; a worker pops it and calls perform.
Args must be JSON-serializable (pass IDs, not objects; symbols become strings).
